name: Maryland
sources: 2026 state brackets incl. new 6.25%/6.5% brackets from Chapter 604, Acts of 2025: Comptroller, '2026 Maryland State and Local Withholding Information' (marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/md/state-payroll/memos/2026/2026-maryland-state-and-local-withholding-information.pdf)

Chapter 604 (BRFA 2025): flat standard deduction indexed after 2025, itemized deductions reduced by 7.5% of FAGI over $200,000, 2% capital gains surtax for FAGI over $350,000, local cap 3.3% from 2026: Comptroller Tax Alert (marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/tax/legal-publications/alerts/tax-alert-changes-to-standard-and-itemized-deductions-and-to-state-and-local-income-tax-rates-from-the-2025-legislative-session.pdf); Form 502CG (2025)

2026 standard deduction $3,400 and exemption table ($3,200, reduced by federal AGI), $1,000 extra for 65+: Comptroller, 2026 Form MW507 instructions (marylandcomptroller.gov/content/dam/mdcomp/md/state-payroll/forms/withholding/2026-instructions-mw507.pdf); 2025 Form 502 line 19

Itemizing: federal Schedule A total less state and local income taxes (2025 Form 502 lines 17a-17c); allowed only if itemized federally (TaxSlayer support; Venable, 'Maryland's Response to the TCJA', 2018); property tax counts up to the federal SALT cap (MSATP)

2026 county rates (3.20% in Baltimore City, Baltimore, Howard, Montgomery, Prince George's and most others; range 2.25%-3.30%): DLS '2026 County Local Tax Rates' (dls.maryland.gov/pubs/prod/NoPblTabPDF/2026CountyLocalTaxRates.pdf)
provisional: Standard deduction for joint/head-of-household filers ($6,800) is inferred as twice the published 2026 single amount ($3,400); the 2026 Form 502 instructions are not yet published
Property-tax cap uses the 2026 federal SALT cap ($40,400; $20,200 separate); its reduction for income over $505,000 is not applied
notes: Includes county income tax at 3.2%, the rate in Baltimore City and most counties (Montgomery, Prince George's, Baltimore, Howard); county rates range from 2.25% to 3.3%.
Maryland cuts itemized deductions by 7.5% of federal AGI over $200,000 ($100,000 separate); this is not applied, so tax may be understated for high-income itemizers.
The 2% capital-gains surtax (federal AGI over $350,000) is applied only to gains above about $350,000 of taxable income, so it can be understated just over that level.
